original_question: Consider the Γ̄q structure γ on the manifold SO(q) whose microfoliation is the suspension of the canonical action of SO(q) on Rq . Is γ null-homotopic in B Γ̄q ?
target_in_paper: Section 9.1, Question 9.2 (Hurder-Vogt): the paper asks whether the specific smooth \overline{\Gamma}_q-structure \gamma on SO(q), whose microfoliation is the suspension of the canonical (standard linear) action of SO(q) on \mathbb{R}^q, is null-homotopic in B\overline{\Gamma}_q. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's official formulation: it has the correct manifold SO(q), the correct \overline{\Gamma}_q-structure \gamma, the correct construction via the suspension of the canonical action of SO(q) on \mathbb{R}^q, and the correct null-homotopy question in B\overline{\Gamma}_q. It is essentially a near-verbatim restatement of Question 9.2. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
missing_details: The paper is working in the smooth (C^\infty) setting in Section 9.1, and your draft does not state that ambient regularity explicitly. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

To be stand-alone, the question should say what a \overline{\Gamma}_q-structure means here: namely, a codimension-q Haefliger structure with trivial normal bundle M\times\mathbb{R}^q. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

It helps to quantify q explicitly (the paper discusses these spaces for each integer q\ge 0, while the question is intended uniformly in q). For the SO(q) formulation, q\ge 1 is the natural nontrivial range. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

For full precision, 'null-homotopic in B\overline{\Gamma}_q' should be unpacked as a statement about the classifying map SO(q)\to B\overline{\Gamma}_q determined by \gamma. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

The paper itself gives an official equivalent reformulation using a \overline{\Gamma}_q-structure \bar\gamma on SO(q)\times[0,1] whose restriction at t=0 is trivial and whose restriction at t=1 is \gamma; including this makes the problem fully concrete. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
refined_question: For a fixed integer q\ge 1, in the smooth (C^\infty) category, let \gamma be the codimension-q Haefliger \overline{\Gamma}_q-structure on SO(q) with trivial normal bundle SO(q)\times\mathbb{R}^q whose microfoliation is the suspension of the standard linear action of SO(q) on \mathbb{R}^q. Is the associated classifying map SO(q)\to B\overline{\Gamma}_q null-homotopic? ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, does there exist a smooth \overline{\Gamma}_q-structure \bar\gamma on SO(q)\times[0,1] whose restriction over SO(q)\times\{0\} is the trivial \overline{\Gamma}_q-structure (with microfoliation given by the slice foliation of SO(q)\times\mathbb{R}^q parallel to SO(q)) and whose restriction over SO(q)\times\{1\} is \gamma? ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
justification: The draft is targeting Question 9.2, not a broader neighboring problem. Section 9.1 first fixes the smooth setting and defines \Gamma_q-structures via microfoliations, with \overline{\Gamma}_q-structures being those with trivial normal bundle; that context is needed to make the question self-contained. The exact Hurder-Vogt problem is then stated on page 31, followed immediately by the paper's own concrete equivalent reformulation on SO(q)\times[0,1]. The paper also notes that the answer is known for q\le 4 and records a weaker related question about whether every homotopy group \pi_p(SO(q)) maps trivially into \pi_p(B\overline{\Gamma}_q), but those are surrounding remarks rather than the primary target. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

citations.label: Remark: positive answer for q\le 4 and weaker homotopy-group variant
